facts.title: ISRO Launches NVS-03 to Strengthen India’s NavIC
facts.headline: A new navigation satellite is an important step toward improving India’s homegrown navigation system.
facts.description: ISRO successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket from Sriharikota on 30 October 2026. NVS-03 is part of India’s NavIC system, which provides positioning, navigation, and timing services across India and nearby regions. The satellite is designed to help improve the availability and continuity of NavIC. However, one successful launch does not by itself guarantee that the entire constellation is fully operational: the satellite must complete post-launch operations and be validated for service, and further satellites are needed to strengthen the system

facts.title: Mussel Inspired Surgical Glue
facts.headline: Researchers have developed flexible adhesives that can stick to wet, moving tissue
facts.description: Surgical adhesives must work in challenging conditions: living tissue is wet, flexible, and constantly moving. Researchers have developed bio-inspired adhesives designed to stick to wet tissues and remain flexible as they move. In a published study, a tough adhesive inspired by slug mucus sealed a defect in a pig’s heart—even while the heart was beating. The work could help inspire future surgical sealants, but it should not be described as a routine, approved treatment for human heart surgery.

facts.title: ISRO Tests a Critical Gaganyaan Spacecraft Separation System
facts.headline: A key safety system for India's human spaceflight mission passes ground tests.
facts.description: On 16 October 2026, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced the successful completion of a series of Crew Module–Service Module separation tests for its Gaganyaan programme. The tests simulated the separation process, including the disconnection of electrical and fluid connections between the two modules. Before the spacecraft's crew module re-enters Earth's atmosphere, it must separate from the service module. The tests also assessed the shock-survivability of critical crew-module systems. This milestone supports preparations for Gaganyaan's first uncrewed mission, targeted for 2026; it does not mean that a crewed mission has already flown.

facts.title: A New Crater Has Appeared on the Moon!
facts.headline: A huge lunar crater was created by an asteroid-sized impact.
facts.description:
NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter detected a new crater named McGetchin on the Moon. A comet or asteroid estimated to be about 10–20 metres (30–60 feet) across struck the lunar surface sometime between April and May 2024. The resulting crater is roughly two soccer fields across, and craters of this size are expected only about once every 132 years.
Source: NASA / NASA GSFC / Intuitive Machines

facts.title: Gel Conversion
facts.headline: A Gell that turns Brain Cell into Neurons
facts.description: For years, one of the most frustrating facts in neuroscience has been this. Once your brain loses neurons, it basically doesn't get them back. The adult brain can make a few new ones here and there, but nowhere near enough to fix the kind of damage that diseases like Alzheimer's cause. So researchers have spent a long time trying to find a workaround, some way to convince the brain to grow replacement neurons on demand

facts.title: A day on Venus is longer than its year
facts.headline: Venus spins incredibly slowly.
facts.description: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once on its axis, while it takes about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

facts.title: Plants can warn their neighbors
facts.headline: Some plants communicate through chemical signals.
facts.description: When attacked, plants can release airborne chemicals that influence nearby plants and can help them prepare defensive responses.

facts.title: Light can behave like a wave and a particle
facts.headline: Light has a remarkable dual nature.
facts.description: Experiments show that light displays both wave-like and particle-like behavior, a key idea in quantum physics.
